answer: right so this question points up another thing to me. we have a requirements file now for all intents and purposes. our intentions. many of them have whys. really every one of them needs a why. and every test case where it's not completely f****** clear what it's testing needs a why. if the point is to change the test case, yeah, the why should make that clear and it should be allowed. and all this stuff that's measuring who's doing what, whether it's which builder (they're currently all you) or what is kinda silly. all we care about really is: does it meet the intentions. the inspectors and gates are what should be measuring that: is it clear that this meets the intentions. if we edit the ticket to better meet the intentions, that's nothing but a good thing and it should be supported by downstream activities if the whys make it clear you're not trying to pull a fast one on yourself. see what i mean?
